<thought>Based on the mass spectrum (M+ at ~199 Da with an M+2 pattern consistent with two sulfurs) and the 13C NMR (four distinct aromatic carbons indicating a para‑disubstituted benzene, plus two aliphatic carbons around 40 ppm typical of –CH₂– attached to heteroatoms), the most plausible structure is para‑bis(2‑mercaptoethyl)benzene (a benzene ring bearing two –CH₂CH₂SH groups opposite each other). The neutral formula C₁₀H₁₄S₂ gives an [M+H]⁺ of ~199 Da, matching the observed mass. The SMILES for this molecule is “SCCc1ccc(cc1)CCS”.</thought>
<final_answer>SCCc1ccc(cc1)CCS</final_answer>
